newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-CESAR FACES FINE FOR LATE RETURN TO DORTMUND.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CESAR FACES FINE FOR LATE RETURN TO DORTMUND.

text.p: Brazilian defender Julio Cesar faces the highest fine in the history of German champions Borussia Dortmund after extending his Christmas holiday without permission, club manager Michael Meier said on Monday.

Cesar's late return to training during the Bundesliga's winter break is becoming an annual ritual -- he has turned up late three times in three years -- and Meier said the fine this time would be a hefty 30,000 marks ($20,000).

Cesar spent some of the break undergoing and recovering from a cartilage operation, but that cut little ice with coach Ottmar Hitzfeld, who said the team had resumed training nine days later than most of their rivals.
"I'm very disappointed with his conduct," Hitzfeld said. "After his injury he could do with the training. As usual, he will be making his contribution to team coffers."
